claims.text: The HEAs considered have a random atomic distribution.
The HEAs considered have significant lattice distortions.
Conventional solid-solution alloys provide an appropriate baseline for comparison with HEAs.
Severe lattice distortions trigger localized nano-twinning during high-strain-rate deformation.
Lattice distortions generate heterogeneous or inhomogeneous local stress fields.
The heterogeneous stress fields caused by lattice distortion favor nano-twin nucleation.
Impeded dislocation motion due to nano-twins increases strain hardening.
Nano-twin-mediated strain hardening maintains ductility while increasing strength.
Under high-strain-rate loading, HEAs will develop a significantly higher nano-twin density than conventional alloys.
Under high-strain-rate loading, HEAs will exhibit greater strain hardening than conventional alloys.
Conventional alloys deform by more uniform dislocation glide than HEAs under comparable high-strain-rate conditions.
The conventional-alloy baseline has lower lattice distortion and minimal nano-twinning under comparable strain-rate conditions.
The proposed mechanism should hold only for HEAs with sufficient lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to HEAs with minimal lattice distortion.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under low-strain-rate, quasi-static conditions.
The quantitative relationship between nano-twin density and strain-hardening magnitude may depend on alloy composition and processing history.
HEAs and conventional alloys should be tested under identical high-strain-rate and temperature conditions while measuring stress-strain response, nano-twin formation, and dislocation density.

Failure to observe both a statistically significant increase in nano-twin density and corresponding enhanced strain hardening in HEAs relative to the conventional-alloy control would falsify the hypothesis.
